messages:
maria: hey team — I uploaded a perfetto trace from the 50k qps e2e run where tail latency jumped at ~14:12 UTC. link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/6a7b9c (shared via perf-bot)

dan: saw that. initial glance: lots of small kernel swaps during long-running requests, looks like runtime is bouncing between quantized and fp kernels mid-request

sachin: interesting — I also noticed a cluster of KV cache misses aligned with those swaps. could be eviction thrash + kernel selection fallback

lia: can you paste the span waterfall? the trace viewer is noisy on my laptop

maria: pasted snippet from perfetto timeline (filtered for client->gateway->runtime):

```
client.send -> gateway.recv -> gateway.dispatch
  gateway.enqueue(batch=8) -> runtime.kv_lookup
    runtime.kv_miss -> runtime.kv_fetch_async
      runtime.kernel_select(quant_fp_check)
        runtime.kernel_launch(gemm_q8)
      runtime.kernel_switch(gemm_fp32)  <-- repeated 3x in 120ms
  gateway.return
```

dan: kernel_switchs occurring while KV fetch still inflight — that causes the runtime to launch a cheaper kernel then immediately switch to fallback when KV arrives. wasteful and explains CPU/GPU thrash

sachin: I ran nsys on a repro with the same seed. command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt -o nsys_hotpath ./run_e2e_load --qps=50000 --seed=42
```
The NVTX shows kernel launch spikes at the same timestamps as perfetto's kernel_switch events

maria: thanks. two hypotheses:
- heuristic in kernel selector is using stale sequence-length distribution while batch is being adjusted -> wrong kernel choice
- KV cache prefetch is racing, and the selector's quantization check is querying approximate token densities which are invalid during partial batch assembly

lia: can we reproduce with a deterministic batch assembly? maybe force batch size and disable autoscale to see if selector still flips

dan: I forced batch_size=8 and disabled autoscale — trace shows far fewer switches but still a handful when KV misses occur. so it's not purely autoscale jitter

sachin: attaching short nvprof flame excerpt (converted to text):
```
Time(ms)  Kernel
0-5       gemm_q8
6-9       memcpy H2D
10-18     gemm_fp32
19-20     kernel_sync
```
pattern repeats per request

maria: propose fix: delay kernel selection decision until KV fetch completes for requests that are KV-dependent OR use speculative selection but pin until KV outcome known. which is cheaper?

dan: pinning would increase latency when KV hits are known early; delaying selection wastes cycles if KV is likely a hit. maybe add cheap prefetch predictor: if KV miss probability > 20% delay, else speculatively choose quantized kernel

lia: can we add a tracing tag to mark "selector_confidence" in the perfetto spans? would help analytics

maria: yup I'll add NVTX push/pop with selector-confidence and kv-state (pending/hit/miss). small change, low risk. I'll run a canary with that tag and post a new trace.

perf-bot: deploy: canary/runtime-selector-confidence-annotate started by maria — CI ok, rolling to 5% of runtime fleet

sachin: one more datapoint — on machines with older CUDA drivers we saw a slightly longer penalty for kernel_switch; driver version should be included in traces

maria: good call. adding driver/cuda version to the trace metadata. thanks all — I'll follow up with the annotated trace and a short PR

lia: :thumbsup: please also add a small eval set that exercises KV-miss-heavy prompts so Optimize can score perf vs quality tradeoffs

maria: will do. next steps posted in #eng-runtime-kanban.
